findings.text: follow-on: plan §2 done-when asks for a directory that 'passes tokamap-validator for the five first-pass groups' (the plan's §1 diagram names them pf_active, pf_passive, wall, tf, magnetics), but the delivered evidence validates four IDS groups only — those the packaged MAST catalogue binds (magnetics, pf_active, pf_passive, wall); the tf group is absent. The exporter filters by the binding's Data Dictionary prefix and is group-agnostic, so it would emit a fifth group from a catalogue that binds one; the shortfall is in the demonstration catalogue, not in the code path. But as delivered the five-group clause is not demonstrated, and a reader of the fragment's 'all four IDS groups the MAST map binds' should not take the plan's five-group clause as satisfied. Closing it needs a catalogue (JT-60SA) with a fifth-group binding and a recorded five-group validator run. This is the same clause the node flags in its own manifest follow_ons.

minor, evidence integrity: the fragment's negative-control line reads 'omitting the COCOS factor ... (1 failed, 4 passed; exit 1)', but the run's cited negative_control.log at the same head 5a07dd95 reads '1 failed, 5 passed in 2.92s' and the test file defines six tests, so the fragment's tally is stale by one — it was not updated when the sixth test (test_group_keys_are_relative_and_verbatim) landed at head. The control itself fires correctly (the COCOS-dependent binding fails with 1.0 vs expected -1.0), so only the quoted passed-count is wrong; correcting it to '1 failed, 5 passed' would make the fragment reconcile with the log it cites.
